meta.title: Tariffs and the cost of building homes: tariffs in force, price changes and production
meta.method: Curated, not a feed. Each tariff and production record was read from its own source on the check date, and its quote is copied from that source. verification.level "primary" means a government notice or agency data release; "reported" means a named law-firm, trade-association or news page. Price changes are not quotes: they are computed by scripts/policy/build_tariffs_brief.mjs from the Bureau of Labor Statistics Producer Price Index values stored in prices[].index (not seasonally adjusted, read from FRED on the check date). The baseline month is the last month before the 2025 tariffs began.
meta.renter_owner: Material costs apply to every new home, rental or for sale. In income-restricted rental homes the rent is capped, so renters do not pay the increase; it becomes funding gap for the building. Buyers of new for-sale homes can see it in the price.

illustration.materials_share_is: A COHO assumption, not a sourced figure: materials as a share of a construction contract, the rest being labor, equipment, overhead and profit.
illustration.rise_low_label: Building materials without energy, one year (NAHB from BLS data)

rise_low_source.title: Building Material Price Inflation Remains High Despite Energy Price Declines
rise_low_source.publisher: National Association of Home Builders, Eye On Housing
rise_low_source.quote: Building material prices were up 0.5% in October and up 5.8% compared to one year ago.

illustration.rise_high_label: Goods used in apartment construction, with fuel, one year (BLS)

known_gaps: No source separates how much of each price increase is tariff and how much is the fuel and freight cost of the war. This brief reports both and does not split them.
Producer price indexes track what US producers charge nationally. They are not Colorado prices and not what a builder pays after markups and delivery.
The materials share of a contract (40% to 50%) is a COHO assumption. A real bid will differ by building type.
The tariff rate now charged on finished appliances was not confirmed against the current federal product list, so this brief gives the price series only.
The Denver cost index covers non-residential building. It is used as the nearest public Colorado measure, not as an apartment cost index.
A plan to restart idled aluminum smelting in South Carolina by June 30, 2026 was announced in August 2025. This brief did not confirm it was finished.
Housing starts fell for several reasons at once, including interest rates, fuel and labor. The data cannot show how much was tariffs.

tariffs.title: Steel, aluminum and copper products
tariffs.rate: 50% of the full value. 25% for goods partly made of these metals. 10% if the metal was made in the US.
tariffs.since: Rates of up to 50% began in 2025, and are charged on full value since April 6, 2026.

source.title: CSMS # 68253075 - Guidance: Section 232 Duties on Imports of Aluminum, Steel, and Copper
source.publisher: U.S. Customs and Border Protection
source.quote: This proclamation imposes 10-50% additional duties on the full customs value of certain imports of steel, aluminum, copper articles (metal articles) and their derivatives from all countries, effective April 6, 2026.

more_sources.title: U.S. Adjusts Section 232 Metal Tariffs
more_sources.quote: Products that are made entirely or almost entirely of aluminum, steel, or copper pay a flat 50% on their full customs value.

more_sources.title: U.S. Adjusts Section 232 Metal Tariffs
more_sources.quote: Derivative articles substantially made of steel, aluminum, or copper pay a flat 25% on their full customs value.

more_sources.title: U.S. Copper Imports Subject to 50% Tariff
more_sources.quote: 50% tariff applies to semi-finished copper products and copper-intensive derivatives Effective August 1, 2025

tariffs.title: Electrical grid equipment and some heating and cooling equipment

source.title: U.S. Adjusts Section 232 Metal Tariffs
source.publisher: GHY International
source.quote: 15% transitional rate: Metal-intensive industrial equipment and electrical grid equipment through December 31, 2027, to support the ongoing US industrial base buildout.

more_sources.title: President Trump Modifies Section 232 Tariffs on Aluminum, Copper and Steel Imports
more_sources.quote: The modified tariff rates went into effect on June 8, 2026, and will expire on December 31, 2027.

tariffs.title: Softwood lumber from Canada
tariffs.rate: 34.75% for most mills: 24.75% in trade duties plus the 10% lumber tariff.
tariffs.since: Duties were cut from 35.16% in October 2026.
tariffs.next: The next yearly duty review is under way

source.title: Softwood lumber recent developments: final results of the seventh administrative reviews
source.publisher: Global Affairs Canada

more_sources.title: U.S. Cuts Duties on Canadian Lumber
more_sources.quote: Total duties on lumber imports are 34.75%, however, because the Trump administration imposed a separate 10% tariff on timber and softwood lumber after a Section 232 national security investigation.

more_sources.title: Softwood lumber recent developments: sixth administrative review amended final results

source.title: Softwood lumber recent developments: United States delays Section 232 tariff rate increase on certain wood products
source.publisher: Global Affairs Canada
source.quote: 10% global tariff on imports of timber (logs) and softwood lumber;

source.title: Softwood lumber recent developments: United States delays Section 232 tariff rate increase on certain wood products
source.publisher: Global Affairs Canada
source.quote: 25% global tariff on kitchen cabinets and vanities, which will increase to 50% on January 1, 2027.

more_sources.title: President Trump Delays Section 232 Tariff Increase on Wood Furniture, Cabinets and Vanities
more_sources.quote: President Trump has delayed for one year – until January 1, 2027 – an increase to 50% of these Section 232 tariffs. The tariff rates will remain at 25%.

tariffs.title: Most other imports
tariffs.rate: 10% or 12.5%. Goods that qualify under the US, Mexico and Canada trade agreement are exempt, and so are goods already under a product tariff above.
tariffs.next: More tariffs are under study, with no date

source.title: US Administration Rebuilds Global Tariff Program Under Section 301
source.publisher: Morgan Lewis
source.quote: Effective July 24, 2026, the new duties generally impose tariffs of 10% or 12.5% on imports from 60 trading partners that account for approximately 99.4% of US imports, subject to significant product and country-specific exceptions.

more_sources.title: US Administration Rebuilds Global Tariff Program Under Section 301
more_sources.quote: Exemptions include articles already subject to Section 232 trade measures, including covered steel, aluminum, automobiles, automotive parts, copper products, and certain other products. Certain qualifying goods from Canada and Mexico also remain outside the new duties, including products receiving preferential treatment under the United States–Mexico–Canada Agreement (USMCA).

more_sources.title: US Trade Court Strikes Down Section 122 Tariffs
more_sources.quote: The administration had turned to Section 122 immediately after the U.S. Supreme Court on February 20, 2026, invalidated tariffs imposed under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act.

production.title: Raw steel made in the US
production.result: Up 5.9% this year through November 14, 2026. Mills ran at 79.5% of capacity, against 76.9% a year earlier.

source.title: US raw steel production increases by 6.0 percent - week 46, 2026
source.publisher: SteelOrbis, reporting American Iron and Steel Institute data
source.quote: Adjusted year-to-date production through November 14, 2026, was 83.423 million net tons, at a capacity utilization rate of 79.5 percent. That is up 5.9 percent from 78.748 million net tons during the same period last year, when the capacity utilization rate was 76.9 percent.

production.title: US sawmills
production.result: Capacity fell 6.0% in a year, by a builders' association estimate for early 2026.

source.title: U.S. Sawmill Output Continues to Shrink
source.publisher: National Association of Home Builders
source.quote: Based on the Census Bureau and Federal Reserve data, NAHB estimates that U.S. sawmills' full production capacity fell 6.0% over the year.
